prerequisites: Basic knowledge of production scenarios considering logistical and manufacturing processes.

learning_outcomes.text: Students name and explain scientific working methods in experimental production technology. They are able to compare and illustrate deviations between theoretical calculations and practical experimental results. They can also classify the boundaries between theoretical knowledge and practical implementation and attribute the problems behind them to individual causes.

After completing the module, students know the limits of experimental proof for theoretically describable relationships and thus contrast theory and practice. They present methods of experimental design and integrate them into their work. Students relate scientific methods and findings to their practical experimental work and organize their approach accordingly in the experimental investigations and illustrate this appropriately.

Students evaluate current scientific findings and combine them with their experimentally obtained results. In doing so, they raise new research questions and formulate initial hypotheses to explain deviations. Working on the assigned tasks in a team promotes the critical reflection of all findings and conclusions at a scientific level.

syllabus_topics: Experiments/laboratory tests in the various laboratories of production technology.

assessment_methods.method: Portfolio examination (4 project reports, either written or oral)

assessment_rules: The portfolio examination consists of four elements focusing on the tasks, procedures, and results of the work in the production technology laboratories. It comprises 4 semester-long project reports, which can be designed as written project reports (PSC) or oral project reports (PMU). The total score is 100 points, with a maximum of 25 points achievable for each project report. The specific composition of the portfolio examination from written and oral project reports will be determined by the lecturer at the beginning of the course.
